caption:
SpaceX says it plans a roughly $50 billion AI supercomputing campus in Cochise County, Arizona.
The application was filed under the name Tombstone Resources LLC, and SpaceX's role only came out at a town hall on November 4.
With Starbase in Texas, the plan tops $74 billion. A petition against the Arizona site has about 2,400 signatures.

threads_text: SpaceX wants to build a $50 billion AI campus in the Arizona desert, and the application was filed under the name Tombstone Resources LLC. It promises 1,000 jobs and lower power bills, while 2,400 locals signed a petition against it. Would you vote yes on this in your county?

paragraphs.text: SpaceX said on November 12, 2026, that it plans to invest more than $74 billion in two supercomputing campuses for artificial intelligence, according to Reuters. Roughly $50 billion would go to a campus in Cochise County, Arizona, and more than $24 billion to a facility at the company's Starbase site in Texas.

Reuters reported that SpaceX described the plan as an expansion of its AI computing ambitions alongside its rocket and satellite businesses. The company's AI segment, which went public in June, produced more than half of SpaceX's revenue in the third quarter.

The Arizona application was filed on October 30 under the name Tombstone Resources LLC rather than SpaceX, according to AI Weekly and Teslarati. SpaceX's involvement became public at a town hall at Cochise Elementary School on November 4. Teslarati, citing local station KVOA, reported that a SpaceX representative told residents the other name was used because putting SpaceX on the filing draws attention from outside the county.

The site covers 747 acres near the Willcox Playa, about 80 miles east of Tucson. The application describes up to nine buildings of about 493,000 square feet each, built in four phases of roughly 1.5 gigawatts, for 6 gigawatts of computing capacity at full build. Teslarati reported that the plan includes a 24 gigawatt hour battery system and about $3.6 billion in grid upgrades.

The scale is large even by SpaceX's own standards. The company ended the third quarter with 1.7 gigawatts of nameplate compute, so the Arizona campus alone would be more than three times that, Teslarati noted. An Arizona Republic analysis cited by the outlet found that the finished campus would draw about 2.5 times more power than all data centers in Maricopa County combined.

SpaceX projects about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs in Arizona. The company said it is working with local electric cooperatives and that the project could lower bills for cooperative members by up to 20 percent. The site sits next to the Apache Generating Station, a coal and natural gas plant of about 1 gigawatt that had been slated to retire by 2028, and SpaceX told residents its investment could expand the station to more than 6 gigawatts.

Water is a central issue in the arid county. SpaceX said the campus would use dry cooling, which relies on air instead of water intensive systems, with no planned industrial groundwater use. The application estimates ongoing water use of 7 to 10 acre feet per year, which Teslarati compared to the consumption of 20 to 30 homes.

The project still needs county approval. A petition asking officials to deny the permit has about 2,400 signatures. Written comments are due November 27, and the Cochise County Planning and Zoning Commission has a public hearing scheduled for December 9 in Bisbee. Teslarati reported that construction could begin in March 2027 if the campus is approved, and that the nearby playa is a landing area for federally protected sandhill cranes.
The Texas half of the plan

At Starbase, SpaceX plans to generate its own electricity rather than draw from the public grid. A city notice described a gas fired power plant and supercomputing facility on about 444 acres. SpaceX said the project has generated more than 3,000 construction jobs and will support more than 500 permanent jobs. The Starbase City Commission is due to consider a property tax abatement for the project on December 9, the same day as the Arizona hearing.

For NeuraFeed, the Arizona filing shows how the race for AI computing power is moving into rural counties, where a single campus can outweigh the existing grid. The promises of jobs and lower power bills are SpaceX's own projections, and local officials will weigh them against concerns about energy, water and wildlife.
Watch the December 9 votes in Bisbee and Starbase, which will decide whether either campus can move toward construction.
